messages:
maya: Ran a bring-up of llama2-70b-int8 on staging. Streaming output is truncating mid-sentence whenever our chat template includes the literal token <STOP>. Looks like the runtime emits an EOS right after a subtoken boundary.

maya: Repro steps:
```
# hf -> redwood conversion
python hf_to_redwood.py --model ./llama2-70b --out ./redwood/llama2-70b-quant
# start a streaming request with chat template that ends with '<STOP>'
```
Logs (excerpt):
```
2027-08-10T14:02:11.123Z runtime: got logits, top_id=50256 prob=0.82
2027-08-10T14:02:11.124Z runtime: emitting EOS marker -> stream: close
```

sam: Do we have the tokenizer config.json and the chat template that was used? Wondering if conversion accidentally set eos_token to "" or mapped a special.

maya: Here are snippets from converted files:
```
# chat_template.txt
{{user}}

<STOP>

# tokenizer config.json
{
  "special_tokens_map": {"eos_token": ""},
  "add_eos_token": true
}
```

ben: yep this is suspicious. Our hf_to_redwood converter sets eos_token to "" if add_eos_token is present and no explicit eos_token in HF config. For some tokenizers that means the string "" gets added as an actual special token with a real id (50256 for this bpe vocab), which then conflicts with user-defined stop tokens.

ben: In FP16/day-to-day it didn't hit because the kernel path and kv-cache flushing behave slightly differently; quantization/int8 path's top-k/fused-softmax can amplify small prob differences so EOS wins.

sam: Can you print token ids for the literal <STOP> token? That will prove whether conversion introduced the eos inside it.

maya: Ran tokenizer debug on staging env:
```
>>> tok.encode("<STOP>")
[1187, 50256]
>>> tok.decode([1187,50256])
"<STOP>"
```
(so the tokenizer maps the second subtoken to id 50256 which is our eos)

sam: Yikes. So our stop string contains the eos id as a suffix. When streaming we see that id and the runtime interprets it as EOS -> early close.

maya: Workaround for now: pad stop token with a non-eos whitespace: use " <STOP>" or put stop token in stop_sequences param instead of templating it literally. Verified streaming continues if we avoid having eos id in the emitted tokens.

ben: Longer-term fix options:
- change hf_to_redwood to not insert a literal "" special token when add_eos_token is true but no explicit eos_token provided. Prefer leaving eos_token unset/null.
- add a conversion-time check that tokenizes all chat template stop tokens and warns/errors if any contain current eos id.
- runtime: allow a flag to ignore EOS coming from tokenizer if it appears embedded after a non-boundary token (risky but possible as an emergency toggle).

sam: I can take the conversion change + check. ben, can you add a small runtime flag (suppress_eos_in_stream=true) so we can enable it for the dedicated pool while we roll the converter fix?

ben: Yep. I'll add the runtime toggle behind a feature flag and make it false by default. We'll also add metrics so we can see how often EOS was suppressed.

maya: Filed quick mitigation in staging: replaced chat template literal with stop_sequences param and it fixes the issue. Will create a short regression test for quantized pathways.

ci-bot: Created issue #3426: "converter: avoid injecting empty-string eos special token during hf->redwood conversion" and issue #3427: "runtime: add suppress_eos_in_stream feature flag (int8 fallback)". Links: https://go/repo/issue/3426 https://go/repo/issue/3427

ben: I'll draft the PR for the runtime flag and the metric. sam, assign me on the converter PR review.

sam: Assigned. I'll add a unit test that tokenizes all chat templates in our model catalog and fails CI if they contain the model's eos id.

maya: Thanks. Action items: sam -> converter PR + unit tests, ben -> runtime flag + metric, maya -> regression test for streaming quantized model. Reopen if we hit any other stop-token edgecases. :+1
summary: conversation about HF->Redwood conversion adding empty-string eos token that causes stop token to include eos id; quantized streaming path triggers early termination. Workarounds, mitigation, and action items recorded.
